topline.text: ASCL told Tes its 'scope for negotiation is exhausted' on Ofsted's impact on leader wellbeing; its council met this week to weigh 'more assertive action', and Lucy Powell has written back admitting the system is 'high-stakes and low-trust'.
topline.action: Nothing to action yet, but worth watching closely.

topline.text: NASUWT is demanding the government republish its funding table for the 3.5% teacher pay rise, arguing schools are being left to cover part of it despite ministers' pension-saving claims.
topline.action: Stress-test this term's budget against the funding assumptions NASUWT is disputing.

topline.text: High Storrs became Sheffield's top-rated secondary under Ofsted's new framework, with a 'strong standard' rating across every inspected area.
Sheffield City Council joined a near-90-council scheme to tackle NEET numbers among 16-17 year-olds, days after the city was flagged as having one of England's higher rates.
topline.action: Useful context for careers leads ahead of post-16 destinations conversations.

diary.text: Sheffield's Year 7 secondary school application deadline for September 2027 entry closes.
Teachers' 2026 pay determination document expected to be laid before Parliament (LGA-estimated date).
Final deadline for academies and local authorities to submit autumn school census returns.
Deadline for schools and colleges to request changes to their 2027-28 high needs place numbers.

sections.heading: Ofsted & accountability: ASCL warns 'scope for negotiation is exhausted'

items.lede: ASCL's council met this week to decide on 'more assertive action' over Ofsted's impact on leader wellbeing.
items.body: General secretary Pepe Di'Iasio said negotiation had been exhausted; Powell responded in writing that the current system is 'high-stakes and low-trust' and that she wants one that is 'more supportive'.
items.action: Worth watching — a union escalation could pull any framework change forward.

sections.heading: Funding: a pay-funding row, and a high-needs deadline to note

items.lede: NASUWT says the 3.5% teacher pay rise isn't funded the way ministers claim.
items.body: The union argues pension-scheme savings cited by Powell were already built into school budgets, so schools may have to find the money themselves; it wants the original funding table republished.
items.action: Check this term's budget against the funding assumptions NASUWT is disputing.

items.lede: Schools and colleges must request any 2027-28 high needs place changes by 6 November.
items.body: This week's DfE Update confirms that if no request is made, 2026-27 place numbers simply roll over and set next year's funding allocation.
items.action: Confirm with your SENCo and finance lead whether specialist place numbers need updating.

sections.heading: Sheffield: a top Ofsted rating and a new NEET action plan

items.lede: High Storrs is now Sheffield's best-rated secondary under Ofsted's stricter framework.
items.body: The Bents Green school, run by Minerva Learning Trust, was praised for pupils' confidence, extracurricular clubs, leadership and above-average attendance.

items.lede: Sheffield has signed up to a near-90-council scheme to tackle NEET numbers.
items.body: The move brings councils, schools, colleges, employers and health services together after figures showed one of England's higher NEET rates among 16-17 year-olds locally.
items.action: Worth a word with your careers lead about how the scheme touches post-16 transition tracking.
